subject: (1,1)-entry of cholesky factor of the correlation matrix equals one

messages.author: 077be7d21770b72d
messages.subject: (1,1)-entry of cholesky factor of the correlation matrix equals one
parts:
If I plot the HMC chain of sampled (1,1)-entries of the cholesky factor of a correlation matrix, they remain constant at one. 

Question 1: Is this expected?

I am under the impression that this is indeed expected. My reasoning goes as follows. A correlation matrix Omega is positive semi-definite, and so its Cholesky factor L is not unique. Constraining one element of L to equal unity makes makes L identifiable, and so the (1,1)-entry of L is constrained to equal unity.

Question 2: Is this reasoning correct?

[I think this question is general enough to not require code, but if I am wrong, let me know and I will post something.]

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] (1,1)-entry of cholesky factor of the correlation matrix equals one
parts:
The requirement is that each row of the Cholesky factor L
must have Euclidean length 1 so that the diagonal of the
correlation matrix is 1. And the diagonal of the Cholesky
factor must also be positive. Together, these are both necessary and
sufficient.

- Bob
